sentences: You're standing at the Church of Saint Anne, the collegiate church of the university.
It is one of the leading examples of Polish Baroque architecture, designed by Tylman van Gameren.
Yet the church's history goes back to the 14th century.
The church was first mentioned in 1381.
In 1407 a fire destroyed it completely, and King Władysław Jagiełło rebuilt it the same year in the Gothic style.
The king also bound the church to the university, giving it the right to name the parish priest.
In 1535 it was raised to the rank of a collegiate church.
In 1689 the Gothic church was pulled down, because it had become too small.
It could no longer hold the growing cult of Saint John Cantius, the patron saint of the university, who is buried here.
From 1689 to 1705 the new Baroque church was built, modelled on Sant'Andrea della Valle in Rome.
Its architect was a Dutchman who had become Polish, the chief architect of the royal court.
Inside, in the transept, you will find the tomb of John Cantius.
Before you walk on, look up at the Baroque church and picture the smaller Gothic one it replaced.

sentences: You're standing at the Church of the Holy Trinity, known to locals as the Dominicans Church.
Built in the Gothic style, it also houses a monastery of the Order of Preachers.
The Dominicans came to Kraków in 1222, with Saint Hyacinth at their head.
The bishop of Kraków gave them the old parish church of the Holy Trinity, and it was consecrated in 1223.
They began to build the new Gothic church and monastery after an invasion in 1241.
Saint Hyacinth is buried here, and so is the Polish ruler Leszek the Black, who died in 1288.
In the chancel lies the bronze tomb plate of the humanist Filip Kallimach, who died in 1496.
It was made to a design by Wit Stwosz.
A free-standing brick bell tower once stood in front of the church.
The great city fire of 1850 left only its burnt walls, and they were taken down.
The same fire burned out the whole interior, except some chapels, and the vault of the nave collapsed.
Rebuilding took decades, and in 1884 the church was consecrated again.
Before you walk on, look at the Gothic portal of the main entrance, sheltered by a later porch.

claims.quote: The then 36-year-old first university in Poland, known at the time as Akademia krakowska (English: the Krakow Academy), moved into the building some time in the 14th century after King Władysław II Jagiełło had purchased it as an educational grant with funds bequeathed by his late wife, Queen Jadwiga.

claims.text: rebuilt in the late 15th century as late Gothic around a large arcaded courtyard
claims.quote: The Collegium Maius was rebuilt in the late 15th century as a late-Gothic structure surrounding a large courtyard bordered with arcades.

claims.text: a well built in the centre of the courtyard in 1517
claims.quote: In 1517 a well was built in the center of the courtyard.

claims.text: professors lived and worked upstairs, lectures downstairs
claims.quote: Professors lived and worked upstairs, while lectures were held downstairs.

claims.text: Nicolaus Copernicus was a student in the 1490s; the Renaissance astronomer who would revolutionize European ideas about the universe
claims.quote: In the 1490s the Collegium Maius counted among its students Nicolaus Copernicus, the Renaissance astronomer and polymath who would revolutionize European ideas about the universe.

claims.text: the Copernicus statue stood in the Collegium Maius courtyard and was moved to the Planty in 1953
claims.quote: It originally stood in the courtyard of the Jagiellonian University's Collegium Maius. In 1953 it was moved to Kraków's Planty Park

claims.text: location of the Jagiellonian University Museum
claims.quote: Collegium Maius is the location of the Jagiellonian University Museum
